# 1.2.81 - tunnels and stairs both ways or one way, a drag onto a tunnel's end, and the owner's 1.2.80 table fixes

Stage E85 in full: H81, the owner's smoke of 1.2.80 at a table on 20.10.2026, fixed but for its one-way case, which is still
open (Known gaps). Tunnels and stairs are read at the token's height and go back the way they came, a GM can make one go one
way, and a token dragged onto a tunnel's end goes through it. The look items of that smoke are fixed too: the roll window's
title, a found room's reveal, the voice tile's word, the sheet's sidebar and Frisk's rows. No other stage is in this version.
None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps).

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **Tunnels and stairs you already have go both ways.** A tunnel whose row names no direction is read as going both ways; a GM
   makes one go one way in **Room setup** > **Passages** (At the table, for the GM).
3. **A token dragged onto a tunnel's end now goes through it.** When the token's student knows the tunnel, a player's drag onto
   the end's mark or a GM's drag onto the end's square takes the token to the far end once it stops, at a door's price, as
   **Go through** does. A GM who drags such a token onto a tunnel's end to place it there sends it through. A move that Foundry
   marks as a teleport goes nowhere; whether Foundry 14 marks a GM's own teleport so has not been checked at a table
   (LIVE-H81-03).
4. **Stairs write the floor's height.** A crossing to another floor writes that floor's bottom as the token's height, with the
   floor; this height was chosen, not read off Foundry 14. A token that 1.2.80's stairs left upstairs at height 0 is read at its
   own height for its tunnel's ends, their marks and the passages in walls.
5. **Settings, keys and texts.** No new setting and no new keybinding. `lang/en.json` goes from 3693 to 3704 strings (11 added,
   none removed, 2 reworded), `lang/pl.json` from 4488 to 4499 (11 added, none removed, 3 reworded). Reworded: a crossing
   refused away from a tunnel's end reads "Stand on the passage's mark, or a square next to it, first." where it read "Your
   character is not at an end of that passage.", the Palm window's Frisk row reads "See what they carry" where it read "Frisk:
   see what they carry", and in Polish the Palm action's hint ends "zobacz, co nosi.".

## At the table

### For the GM

- Under a tunnel's Shape in **Room setup** > **Passages** there is a choice, "Both ways" or "Only from {from} to {to}", with both
  directions offered and the rooms named as the row names them.
- The choice is written at once and logged, and the players whose students know the tunnel get the change.
- Only a GM writes it, and only for a tunnel or stairs; the tab's footnote says "A tunnel or stairs can go one way only: pick it
  under its Shape. A passage in a wall always goes both ways."
- The primary GM judges the direction from the GMs' own record, and **Go through** from the other end is refused with "This
  passage cannot be taken from this side."
- The Mastermind is held to a tunnel's direction too, and a season's reset and a room's rename keep it.
- The **At season start** column's header carries "Known again after each season reset. Adding a student here does not give them
  the passage now." as its tooltip, and the tab's footnote says it too.
- A GM's drag of a student's token onto a tunnel end's square takes it through, as a player's drag onto the mark does (For a
  student who knows a passage). A GM's board draws no mark: **Show** on the passage's row in the Passages tab shows where it is.
- A Monokuma's token goes through no tunnel by a drag, as its sheet lists no **Known passages**.
- Where the GMs are putting the token back, hold it as standing where the rules refuse, or saw it move while the price was taken,
  the primary GM now refuses the crossing with "That cannot be done now."; 1.2.80 refused these three as a token not at an end.
  The primary GM's console warning for the refused request names which of the three it was.
- **Verbose console logging** is each browser's own setting, so the GM and the player each turn it on (LIVE-H81-01). With it on,
  a crossing refused away from an end writes a Debug line in the console of the browser that asked, naming every end with its
  floor and room as the token's height reads it, and the primary GM writes one for each of the three causes above.

### For a student who knows a passage

- **Drag your token onto a tunnel's mark** to go through it, or stand on the mark or a square next to it and press **Go through**
  under **Known passages**; either way it costs what a door costs, and the same refusals turn you back in the same words.
- The drag counts when the token's centre square ends on the mark, from a start off it, and the crossing starts once the token
  stops. A drag that ends beside the mark or runs across it goes nowhere, and so does a move that only climbs, turns or changes
  floor.
- A token the module places itself goes nowhere either: the gathering of everyone at a body, the cast placed at a new season or
  after a trial, a body moved by a clean-up, a put-back and the crossing's own landing.
- A drag and a press of **Go through** at the same moment ask once, and with no action left a drag says "No Free Move and no
  actions left." once.
- A tunnel or stairs goes back the way it came: from where the crossing lands you, **Go through** takes you back, on one floor
  and up and down stairs between two floors.
- The end you stand at is read at your token's height, and the far end and the landing at the height you will stand at there.
  At 1.2.80, on a model of Foundry 14's regions, the upper end of stairs over a room drawn with no floor read as the room under
  it where the upper room's name sorts first: the way back from it was refused and its mark was not drawn.
- **Go through** stays enabled wherever your token stands; pressed away from an end it says "Stand on the passage's mark, or a
  square next to it, first."
- A one-way tunnel says so under its name, "One way only: from {from} to {to}.", and its other end stays marked for you,
  captioned "Secret passage from {room}".
- Under a passage in a wall the list says "Walk through the gap in the wall.": its row has no **Go through**, as before.
- A tunnel end's caption is bigger: 0.36 of the grid and at least 20 px, 36 px on a 100 px grid where it was 22, over a thicker
  keyline, just under its ring; how it reads is left to a table.

### For everybody

- **The roll window's title lies flat again.** At 1.2.80 it could stand one letter a line in a header that centres it or sizes it
  to its content; it now takes its header's whole width, and a long title still does not widen the window. This is measured in
  Chromium on a stand-in window with the module's stylesheets alone, without Foundry's or Daggerheart's CSS (LIVE-E16-02).
- **A found room opens at once.** The reveal's curtain starts opening at 400 ms and the room is open at 1100 ms; at 1.2.80 it
  stayed shut until 3150 ms and was open at 5400 ms. The sound still plays as the reveal starts, and the room's name stays up
  for 5.4 s as before.
- **The voice tile's state word stands at the top of the tile, over the picture, and stays while somebody speaks.**
- While a face is shown and voice is connected, the word's tooltip is "Connected to your voice channel.", and the screen
  reader's line is still not rewritten each time a speaker comes or goes.
- Under Monokuma Legacy the word stands beside the top buttons, cut or moving as the ticker does; with the ticker off or reduced
  motion it stands still under the buttons' row.
- Under Stained Glass the word stands at the top in both of the tile's forms, with the speaker's name at the foot.
- On a stacked screen, while somebody speaks, the word stands in a band over the top of the face.
- **On a student's sheet,** what **Known passages** and Daggerheart's Experience hold under their headings takes 10 px of inline
  padding, as the Equipped block's line does; the 10 px is chosen, not measured against Daggerheart's own rows (LIVE-H81-02).
- **Frisk's row** in the Palm window reads **See what they carry**, like the Palm window's other two rows, and in Polish
  **Zobacz, co nosi**. A Frisk's toast is kept in the notice history under the title "Frisk".
- Frisk's **Openly** and **Unseen** choice is drawn as the module's other choice rows: under Stained Glass with their dark cut
  row, strip, brush and radio colour, and under Monokuma Legacy with the Rest picker's hover.

## Changed

- No new file: 149 files in `scripts/`, as at 1.2.80.
- **Tunnels and stairs**: `movement.mjs` (the reads at the token's height, the landing's height, the drag's decision
  `tunnelStepTarget` and the placing mark `whilePlacing`), `rooms.mjs` (`floorElevation`), `passages.mjs`, `passages-gm.mjs`
  (`setPassageWay`, the direction in `crossTunnel`), `passages-tab.mjs`, `sheet.mjs` (the rows' lines and the drag), `fog.mjs`,
  `fog-doorways.mjs`, `fog-reveal.mjs`, `eclipse.mjs`, `gm-bridge.mjs` and `bridge-guards.mjs`; the module's three region
  teleports, in `call-world.mjs` and `cleanup.mjs`, run inside `whilePlacing`.
- **The look**: `fog-reveal.mjs` (the reveal's times), `voice-tile.mjs`, `frisk.mjs`, `styles/danganronpa.css` and
  `styles/stained-glass.css`.
- No bridge action was added: the drag sends the same `passage.cross` request as **Go through**, and the request still carries
  only the character and the passage.
- **Tests**: 10 new numbered tests, R900-R909 (4 in tier 0: R905, R906, R907 and R909; 6 in tier 1: R900 to R904 and R908);
  next free R910.
- R558, R588, R589, R602, R603 and R620, and the census rows of R379, R432, R472 and R553, changed with them.
- Two more tier-2 tests, which carry no number: "H81-01 stairs" and "H81 C3 drag" (954 titles in `scripts/tests-tier2.mjs`, 952
  at 1.2.80). A10-18 reads the three new causes, and the roll window's test reads each title's declared width and the header's
  alignments.
- The scenario files are still 28: scenario 76 gains three checks of a drag (76 U), and scenario 75's check G holds the word kept
  while somebody speaks.
- `known-leaks.json` is unchanged (9 known leaks).
- **The manifest's compatibility is unchanged**: Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` 2.6.5, Foundry `minimum` 14.364 and
  `verified` 14.365.
- The handbooks, in English and Polish: the GM handbook's sections 5 (the Palm row) and 9.6 (the drag onto a tunnel's end, one
  way, what goes nowhere), the player handbook's chapters 3 (where to stand, the drag, one way, the wall's gap) and 4 (Frisk's
  row), and the Polish Student Brochure's Palm line.
- Outside the module: the glass harness and the glass sweep read the voice word beside the face and gain three planted faults
  (`onPlate`, `cramped`, `shortName`), `tools/check.mjs`'s `live` part reads LIVE-H ids, `tools/stages.json` gains the E85 row
  and each unshipped 1.2.X row below it moves up one version (43 rows), `docs/dev/R-REGISTRY.md` gains the ten rows, and the
  audit's section 9.2 gains items 272 to 274.

## Known gaps

- **The owner's one-way case is still open as a defect.** The cause this version fixes is measured on a model of Foundry 14's
  regions only, and only where the upper room's name sorts before the room under it; it may not be what the owner hit. The owner
  said on 21.10 that the case was seen from the GM's browser and that a tunnel between floors must work; on one floor or two,
  and on which scene, is not known. On one floor the harness goes through and back at 1.2.80 as now, so if the case was on one
  floor its cause is still open.
- **LIVE-H81-01** (not tried yet): on a Foundry 14 table, with **Verbose console logging** on for the GM and the player and the
  console's Verbose level shown, a knower goes through a tunnel on one floor and straight back, then up and down stairs, also
  with a token placed upstairs another way and one that 1.2.80's stairs left at height 0; each refusal's words and both
  consoles' lines are written down, with the scene's floors and the two rooms' regions.
- **LIVE-H81-02** (not tried yet): on a real sheet in both themes, how far from the sidebar's edge the Equipped line, the first
  Experience row and the first **Known passages** row stand. Two older readings disagree, so the Experience rows may stand at 17
  px, 7 px further in than the rest, or at 10 px.
- **LIVE-H81-03** (not tried yet): on a Foundry 14 table, a player's and a GM's drag onto a tunnel's end goes through once and
  does not bounce back; a drag beside the mark, a GM's teleport and a change of floor on Foundry's own stairs go nowhere; which
  options Foundry 14 writes on a drag, whether a move comes as one update or several, and whether the module's region teleports
  write before their promise answers.
- LIVE-E16-02 now also asks that the roll window's title lies flat, and LIVE-E79-21 asks how the voice word reads over a face.
- Where a room drawn with no floor lies under a floor's room, a token upstairs stands in the one whose name sorts first, for the
  fog, the doors and the crossings alike; this is unchanged and is a rules decision for the owner.
- The height a crossing writes on another floor, and the Mastermind held to a one-way tunnel, are choices made here, for the
  owner.
- No scenario drives a one-way tunnel through the harness's browsers, so the refusal told on a player's page is not seen; tier 1
  (R901, R902) tests the GMs' road and the copies.
- **Go through** is not drawn disabled away from an end, as the design wanted: nothing redraws the sheet when a token moves, so
  the click's refusal says where to stand.
- The direction's choice wraps to four or five lines in the Passages tab's Shape column; this was drawn in Chromium without
  Foundry's CSS (LIVE-E80-04).
- Which parent Daggerheart's own roll window gives its title, and whether a rule of Daggerheart's sets its width with
  `!important`, is not read: no Daggerheart CSS is on this machine (LIVE-E16-02).
- Whether a 400 ms cut-and-hold and an 1100 ms reveal read well at a table is not judged.
- The sidebar's 10 px is the module's own Equipped line's; a row that Daggerheart already pads stands that much further in.
- Under Monokuma Legacy the word in the 69 px band beside the buttons is cut, and moves only with the ticker on; on a stacked
  screen with nobody speaking, under Legacy, "Disconnected" loses its last letters. The words' widths are the glass harness's
  fonts, and a table's may be wider (LIVE-E79-21).
- On a stacked screen the word's band over a speaker's face is a choice made here, and how the word reads over a real portrait
  is not judged.
- The world setting **Frisk: forcing after a refusal** keeps its name.
- **Known passages** names a wall passage's two rooms at the floor's bottom whatever the token's height; one update that both
  changes a token's height and crosses a wall passage reads both sides at the height it starts from; and a room's outline drawn
  again on a change of passages keeps the height it was drawn at.
- The drag: a second GM's drag onto an end is tested only in the decision (R908) and by the button's road; a put-back of the GMs
  that lands after the ask is read in the code and not driven; where two ends of one tunnel lie within a square of each other, a
  drag onto one may be taken as a crossing from the other, which is not measured.
- A drag that the primary GM refuses with "That cannot be done now." says nothing, which also covers a body nobody has found and
  a far room gone from the GMs' map; the button says it.
- A second ask while one is on its way is dropped without a word, and the row's button is not drawn disabled on other sheets.
- The tunnel's mark cannot be clicked, and the sheet's tunnel row says nothing of dragging; the handbooks say it.
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped are unchanged.
